newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks close down on FII selling, Rao woes.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks close down on FII selling, Rao woes.

text.p: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and bear operators pushed down share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Thursday, dealers said.
They said sentiment was depressed by news that former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao had been denied interim protection against arrest by the Delhi High Court.
The Delhi Stock Exchange fell 9.39 points to close at 727.92 points.
Selective buying by domestic financial institutions could not counter the selling spree, they said.
"In view of tomorrow's end of settlement, operators preferred to reduce their positions," a broker said.
Reliance fell 3.15 rupees to 194, and TISCO lost 2.70 rupees to 170.30, as FIIs unloaded shares.
State Bank of India shed 5.40 rupees to 259.10 on FII selling ahead of the bank's proposed $400 million issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs).
Associated Cement Co, undercut by profit-taking, fell 59 rupees to 1,790.
ITC fell 1.30 rupees to 298.50, while ITC Hotels ended 17 rupees lower at 117.
